solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Pressure surrounding midsummer trade

indicators.note: the pressure word goes round the middle letters, as a wall surrounds a garden
'midsummer' asks for the middle of SUMMER, not the season

blocks.note: to coerce is to pressure someone
the two middle letters of SUMMER

explanation.surface: A merchant leaning on midsummer, the busy season, to push sales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Midsummer' reads as a date, but it is a letter instruction: the middle of the word SUMMER.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both words name the business of buying and selling goods.

clue.text: Otherwise a small group of players includes old musical work

indicators.note: the group of players takes the old letter inside it

blocks.note: or = otherwise, as in 'hurry, or you'll miss it'
O is the standard abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A small ensemble reviving an antique piece of music instead of something else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small group of players' pulls towards a sports team, but these players are musicians, which fits the musical definition at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by class: the answer is a large sacred work for voices and orchestra, like Handel's Messiah, one kind of musical work.

clue.text: Medium is frantically lamenting bad omen in stars?

definitions.note: the question mark flags the astrological reading: stars out of line

indicators.note: letters moving frantically are thrown out of order

blocks.note: M = medium, as on clothing labels
anagram fodder, joined to 'is' across the indicator

explanation.surface: A spiritualist medium wailing over a dire sign read in the heavens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Medium' looks like the fortune-teller herself, but it only gives M; the indicator sits between the two words of its fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Astrologers read planets out of their proper line-up as ill-starred, so the question mark admits a playful, astrology-only sense.

clue.text: Religious teacher with little time for chat

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time; 'little' signals the abbreviation

explanation.surface: A busy rabbi who can spare only a few minutes to talk.
explanation.walkthrough: To rabbit (on) is British slang for talking at length, from the rhyming slang 'rabbit and pork' = talk.
explanation.definitionFit: A British regional sense: the verb means to chatter, usually for too long.

clue.text: For sporting event, one’s tip is modified, to be blunt

definitions.text: For sporting event, one’s tip is modified, to be blunt

blocks.note: one of the three fencing events, named after the sword it is fought with

blocks.clueFragment: one’s tip is modified, to be blunt
blocks.note: reads as 'frankly, it has been altered'; really the sword's point is capped with a button so it is literally blunt

explanation.walkthrough: 'To be blunt' pretends to mean 'to speak frankly', but it describes the competition sword's buttoned point. No part of the clue gives letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue describes the thing itself: a fencing sword whose tip is blunted for sport, which also names its event.

clue.text: Bank covering up failure in negligent way

indicators.note: one word covers the other, so the failure sits inside it

blocks.note: to bank on someone is to rely on them

explanation.surface: A bank hiding its own blunder by sloppy practice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' looks like the financial institution but is the verb, as in 'bank on'.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: remiss means negligent, and the adverb matches the phrase 'in negligent way'.

clue.text: Not top gear for female in car

blocks.note: gear is clothing: a short skirt, worn on the lower half rather than as a top
a small British car first built in 1959

explanation.walkthrough: 'Top gear' suggests fifth gear, or the car programme; here gear means clothes, and the answer is short for miniskirt as well as the classic small car.
explanation.definitionFit: Two nouns sharing one spelling: a short skirt, which is women's clothing but not a top, and the small car made by Austin and later BMW.

clue.text: Mint and nutmeg, initially, put in tea, say

indicators.note: 'initially' keeps only the first letter of nutmeg
the letters are put inside the tea word

blocks.note: tea is one kind of brew, hence 'say'

explanation.surface: A herbal infusion: mint and a pinch of nutmeg stirred into tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mint' sits among spices as a herb, but it is the definition, as in 'in mint condition'.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: goods in mint condition are unused, as fresh as when made.

clue.text: After king hugged by favourite, row becomes less ugly

indicators.note: the king is held inside the favourite, as in an embrace

blocks.note: a teacher's pet is a favourite
a row, as of seats in a theatre

explanation.surface: Once the king is embraced by his favourite, the quarrel turns less nasty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' reads as a quarrel (rhymes with cow), but it is a line of seats (rhymes with go). 'After' puts the favourite-and-king piece first.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by negation: calling something less ugly is a grudging way of saying it has grown more attractive.

clue.text: Fish that gets played? Doesn’t sound like it

blocks.note: a sea or freshwater fish, its name rhyming with mass
a low-pitched instrument, its name said like base

explanation.walkthrough: The second sentence is the setter's aside: the fish and the instrument are spelt the same but pronounced differently, so this is not a homophone clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Two nouns sharing one spelling but not one sound: a fish, and the bass guitar or double bass that a musician plays.

clue.text: RAF, for example, regrouped above Britain

indicators.note: letters regrouped are put in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Air force squadrons re-forming high over Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a wartime air battle; the RAF is the Royal Air Force, and the clue treats its name as letters rather than planes.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: RAF is the short form of Royal Air Force.

clue.text: Innovative attempt mostly transformed tent design

indicators.note: 'mostly' keeps most of the word, dropping its last letter
letters transformed are rearranged into a new form

explanation.surface: A bold experiment that largely reinvented how tents are made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Innovative attempt' reads as one phrase, but 'Innovative' alone defines and 'attempt mostly' gives only two letters to the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A near synonym: something that starts a fashion others follow is by nature new and innovative.

clue.text: Creative skill is put into middle section of smarter essay

indicators.note: IS is placed inside the other letters
only the central letters of smarter are kept

blocks.note: the middle three letters of SMARTER

explanation.surface: Flair inserted into the central part of a sharper piece of writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Essay' looks like a school composition but is the old sense of an attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the word means an artist's creative skill or craft.

clue.text: Long story about what Romeo and Juliet have in common

indicators.note: the story goes round the shared letter

blocks.clueFragment: what Romeo and Juliet have in common
blocks.note: the only letter found in both names

explanation.surface: Someone describing Shakespeare's lengthy tale of what bound the two lovers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long story' pairs naturally, but 'Long' is the verb definition; 'what they have in common' means the letters, not love.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the verb: to long for something is to ache for it.

clue.text: Fresh information sent back about editor in part of Europe

indicators.note: something sent back travels the other way
the turned word goes round the editor

blocks.note: ED is the standard abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: A foreign correspondent's report on a newspaper editor bounced back from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: The news-and-editor surface keeps the reader in a newsroom, far from the map the definition points to.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by class: a Scandinavian country is one part of Europe.

clue.text: E.g. Keats, Milton, or Pope, often

definitions.text: E.g. Keats, Milton, or Pope, often

blocks.note: two English poets, pushing the reader towards POET; what they actually share is a first name
Alexander Pope continues the poets, but the capital P hides a pontiff, and popes have often taken this name

explanation.walkthrough: The list of poets makes POET the obvious guess, and it even fits four letters; 'often' is what kills it, since it only makes sense for popes choosing a name.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by examples: Keats and Milton share the first name, and twenty-odd popes have taken it.

clue.text: Jokes about an East Asian language

indicators.note: the jokes go round the article

explanation.surface: Jokes told about a language of the Far East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'East Asian' reads as one phrase, but 'East' belongs to the wordplay as E and only 'Asian language' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by class: the language of Japan is one of the languages of Asia.

clue.text: Leaders deserting the navy — that’s hard to bear

indicators.note: the first letters of the words walk away, leaving the rest

explanation.surface: Officers abandoning the fleet, a blow the sailors find hard to take.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaders' look like admirals; here they are the first letters of 'the' and 'navy'.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in both senses: a weight or a sorrow that is hard to bear is heavy.

clue.text: What’s tormented flesh or rear of pony?

definitions.text: What’s tormented flesh or rear of pony?

indicators.note: tormented letters are twisted out of order
the rear of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A riddle about some pest that has been plaguing a pony's hide or hindquarters.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: 'tormented' is the anagram indicator and also exactly what the insect does.
explanation.definitionFit: An &lit: read straight, the clue asks what torments a pony's flesh or rump, and this biting fly is exactly that.

clue.text: Returned conflict diamonds in no-win situation

indicators.note: returned letters go back the way they came

explanation.surface: Blood diamonds from a war zone handed back, leaving nobody the winner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conflict diamonds' is a real phrase for gems sold to fund wars, which hides that the words are two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A sporting sense: a game that ends level is a result in which nobody wins.

clue.text: Some heathen I antagonised, European citizen

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the following words are taken

blocks.note: starts at the third letter of 'heathen' and ends two letters into 'antagonised'

explanation.surface: A confession: I have upset a pagan who is a citizen of Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: The run crosses the word breaks, from inside 'heathen' through 'I' into 'antagonised'.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by class: a citizen of the Greek capital is one kind of European citizen.

clue.text: Affected person regrets surgery going the wrong way

indicators.note: letters going the wrong way run backwards

explanation.surface: A patient ruing an operation that went badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Affected person' reads as a patient hit by the surgery; affected here means pretentious.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone who strikes poses to impress is affected, putting on airs.

clue.text: Capital husband invested in modern food store

indicators.note: the husband is placed inside the store, as money is put into a business

blocks.note: H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A husband putting his money into a trendy food shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' and 'invested' make a money story, but capital is a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by class: India's seat of government is one of the world's capitals.

clue.text: Like many cases in court, end in disarray

indicators.note: letters in disarray are jumbled

blocks.note: to court someone is to woo them

explanation.surface: Law cases in court that fall apart at the finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cases in court' reads as lawsuits, but the cases are boxes, and 'court' is the verb for wooing.
explanation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: packing cases and crates are often made of timber, so many are of that material.

clue.text: No short-term changes about name highest in charts?

definitions.note: the question mark flags that 'highest' means top of the map

indicators.note: the letters of short-term change places
the rearranged letters go round the name

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A pop act that stays at number one in the charts for good, no quick turnover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charts' suggests the hit parade, but it means maps, where north is at the top.
explanation.definitionFit: A map convention: north is drawn at the top of a chart, so the point furthest north sits highest on it.

clue.text: Defeat as result of having resistance extinguished

blocks.note: R is the symbol for electrical resistance
a fire that is out has been extinguished

explanation.surface: An army beaten because its resistance movement was crushed.
explanation.walkthrough: R for resistance comes from physics, where it stands for electrical resistance in formulas like V = IR.
explanation.definitionFit: A near synonym, as noun or verb: to defeat utterly, putting the enemy to flight.

clue.text: Name of Parisian embracing right standard

indicators.note: the French word holds the R in its arms

explanation.surface: A Parisian's name taken up by the political right as its banner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Name of Parisian' reads as a person's name; it asks for the French word for name.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the usual level or pattern against which others are measured.

clue.text: Bird nesting in hibiscus

indicators.note: the bird sits inside the next word like a nest in a bush

blocks.note: the four letters straight after the opening h

explanation.surface: A bird building its nest in a hibiscus shrub.
explanation.walkthrough: The indicator is part of the picture: the bird really is nesting in the flowering shrub's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by class: a long-billed wading bird, sacred in ancient Egypt.

clue.text: Runner is more complacent going across line

indicators.note: the word stretches across the line, so the L ends up inside it

blocks.note: smug = complacent, so this is the comparative
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A cocky athlete strolling over the finishing line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' and 'line' paint a race, but a runner is also someone who runs contraband, as in gun-runner.
explanation.definitionFit: A second sense: one who runs goods illegally across borders, like a rum-runner.

clue.text: Chap becoming more mature and coping

explanation.surface: A fellow getting older and handling it well.
explanation.walkthrough: AGING is the American spelling of British ageing; the grid needs the shorter form.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: getting by despite difficulty, as in 'I'm managing fine'.
